searchText: Skipping the tests that won't wrap in an initcontainer is fine. But I think we should throw all other invalid containers individually to each tx pool with a very high priority fee to see which clients attempt to include them. We should also have some 64k+ initcontainers too (multiple 64k sub-containers) This will be good as it flexes the txpool and blockbuilding, which we cannot do in reference tests. <@403707149043105803> I've done some heavy refactoring of Nethermind, it passes all Eof tests; but I have a little worry I may have broke some tracing used in fuzzing (as don't think is test coverage there?). So let me know if so Fuzzing is fine, but one deep fuzzing test broke instantly. I'll need to spend some time reducing it but I'll DM you the raw failed test. Fuzzing is fixed. A real interesting test case was discovered.
